predecessors.name: Tunjur kingdom
predecessors.text: the Maba heartland around Wara and Abéché (the gazetteer's Wadai region inside Cliopatria's outline); the page gives no extent for the first century

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the whole sultanate, 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'

ledger.x: 1635: Abd al-Karim founds the Wadai sultanate by overthrowing the Tunjur.
1804 onward: Sabun extends the sultanate south.
ledger.cp: Dar Sila, Dar Runga and Dar al Kuti peoples (no dossier)

ledger.x: The Bagirmi campaign is a one-year event on the page: no occupation or tribute is described afterwards.
29 May 1908: the first dated French victory over Wadai forces, at Dokotchi.

wars.name: Wadai-Darfur conflicts
wars.outcome: Wadai was a tributary of Darfur through the 17th century; Ya'qub Arus later refused tribute and 'Darfur attacked Wadai but was defeated'; Darfur installed Sharif in Wadai in 1838 and he quickly regained independence.

wars.name: Wadai conquest of Bagirmi
wars.outcome: Wadai defeats Bagirmi, kills its ruler and enslaves 20,000 people (the page); no annexation is described.

wars.name: Wadai War
wars.outcome: French victory: Dokotchi (29 May 1908), Djoua (16 June 1908), Abéché (June 1909); Wadai wins at Wadi Kadja (4 January 1910) and Dorothe (8 November 1910, Maillard killed); Dud Murra surrenders in October 1911; 'completely occupied by the French in 1912'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Wadai frontier; the 1898-1899 Anglo-French division left 'the Wadai-Darfur borders' disputed, and the Sahel edges of the outline are approximate throughout.
